evidence.reason: The finding is a proposal to change an explicitly documented ID scheme, not evidence of an implementation error in intended behavior. The current multi-repo doc states the format and resolves it: push ids `push-<name>-<base10>-<head10>`, PR ids `<name>-pr<n>`, deltas `<name>-pr<n>-range-<pin>-<head>`, and line 76 states "`<name>` is the repo's suffix after `/`." The code building ids from `cfg["name"]` therefore matches the documented design rather than contradicting it. The finding supplies no excerpt of `repo_registry.py` showing that two different owners with the same repo name can actually be enrolled in one queue, and no current-contract clause requires owner-qualified item ids; the phrase "so ids stay unique across repos" is the doc's own scope statement for the suffix scheme. Switching to an encoded `owner/name` slug, including overflow and recovery ids, would enlarge the ID requirement (a migration/design change), which the guidance says is not itself a defect. Nothing here shows an ordinary bug within existing intended behavior.
